data.name: Asareer
data.gender_notes: Asareer is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'asara' meaning 'ten'. This name is given to a child who is the tenth in the family, or who is expected to embark on a journey or a new phase of life. It symbolizes freedom and a sense of adventure. The name Asareer carries the meaning “The One Traveling” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Asareer usually hope their child will grow to embody the one traveling and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies a spiritual journey and the courage to travel the path of life with faith and determination.
data.etymology: Asareer belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “The One Traveling.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asareer total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: أسير
in_arabic.meaning: أسير يعني الشخص المسجون أو المأسور
in_arabic.long_meaning: أسير هو اسم مشتق من الفعل 'أسَرَ' والذي يعني أخذ الشيء أو الشخص بالقوة. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى الشخص الذي يتم أسره أو احتجازه. في سياق تاريخي، كان يتم استخدام هذا الاسم في الحروب والصراعات للإشارة إلى الأسرى. وفي القرآن الكريم، يتم استخدام مشتقات هذا الفعل في عدة آيات لوصف الأسرى والمعتقلين.

in_urdu.name: اسیر
in_urdu.meaning: اسیر مطلب ہے پکڑا ہوا یا قیدی
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسیر ایک نام ہے جو عربی زبان کے الفعل 'أسَرَ' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے زبردستی لینا یا پکڑنا۔ اردو میں، اس نام کا استعمال اس شخص کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے جو پکڑا گیا ہو یا قیدی ہو۔ اس نام کی اہمیت اس کی تاریخی اور ثقافتی سیاق و سباق میں ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیا میں مسلم معاشرے میں۔

in_hindi.name: आसीर
in_hindi.meaning: आसीर का अर्थ है कैदी या बंदी
in_hindi.long_meaning: आसीर एक नाम है जो अरबी भाषा के क्रिया 'أسَرَ' से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है जबरन लेना या पकड़ना। हिंदी में, इस नाम का उपयोग उस व्यक्ति के लिए किया जाता है जो पकड़ा गया हो या कैदी हो। इस नाम का महत्व इसकी ऐतिहासिक और सांस्कृतिक संदर्भ में है, विशेष रूप से भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में।

in_pashto.name: اسیر
in_pashto.meaning: اسیر دى پښتو ژبې معنی قیدی یا نیول شوی
in_pashto.long_meaning: اسیر په پښتو ژبه کې د هغه چا لپاره کارول کیږي چې نیول شوی یا قیدی دی. دا نوم د عربی ژبې د 'أسَرَ' فعل څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې ده زورمنی وړل یا پکڑل. په افغانستان او پښتونستان کې، دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کېږي چې په جګړو او شخړو کې نیول شوي.

in_english.name: Asareer
in_english.meaning: Asareer means prisoner or captive in English
in_english.long_meaning: The name Asareer originates from the Arabic root 'أسَرَ' (asara), which means to take by force or to capture. In English, Asareer translates to 'prisoner' or 'captive'. Historically, this name has been used to refer to individuals captured during wars or conflicts. In Islamic tradition, the concept of being a captive or prisoner is mentioned in the Quran, emphasizing the importance of compassion and justice towards those who are detained.

historical_references.reference: Asareer were a group of Bedouin tribes who lived in the region of Arabia between the Euphrates River and the Arabian Gulf. They were known for their military prowess and were often hired by various Islamic rulers for their services. In the late 7th and early 8th centuries CE, they played a significant role in the expansion of the Umayyad Caliphate under the leadership of their chief, Al-Harith ibn Hisham.

The name 'Asareer' is also mentioned in the works of historians such as Ibn Abd al-Hakam and Ibn Al-Athir in relation to the campaigns of the Abbasid Caliph Harun Al-Rashid against the Byzantines and the Umayyads. During this period, the Asareer were one of the major Bedouin confederations and their support was crucial for the success of Harun's military campaigns in Syria and Iraq.
historical_references.context: Abbasid Caliph Harun Al-Rashid and military campaigns
